clue.text: In great trepidation, chose to include article

indicators.note: picked is told to take the article inside itself

parts.note: chose means picked
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone nervously made a choice that involved adding an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in great trepidation means being overcome with sudden fear or alarm.

clue.text: Springbok's ready to dive in a wee bit haphazardly

indicators.note: the cash is told to plunge into the tiny particle, so it goes inside

parts.note: an atom is a tiny particle, a wee bit
ready money is cash; the rand is the currency of South Africa, home of the Springboks

explanation.surface: A South African rugby player is poised to plunge into something small without much thought.
explanation.walkthrough: A Springbok is a South African (the national rugby team's nickname), and 'ready' is slang for cash, so 'Springbok's ready' is the RAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without plan or method is doing it haphazardly.

clue.text: Children's edition

definitions.meaning: an edition of a magazine is a single number of it

explanation.definitionFit: Offspring is a legal sense of the word, and a printing of a periodical is the other sense.

clue.text: Refuse to be upset, and don't accept wigging?

definitions.meaning: the idiom for staying calm and not losing one's temper
read literally, keeping your own locks rather than wearing a wig; a wigging is also a scolding

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stay calm; read literally it means retain your own natural head covering instead of a wig.

clue.text: Fed up with performance — nothing working effectively?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
an act is a performance
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with a show where nothing seems to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED to DEF; 'working' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in fact or in practice, whatever the official position.

clue.text: Material was touching

definitions.meaning: a fabric made of matted wool
past tense of feel, to touch

explanation.definitionFit: A pressed woollen fabric, and also the past tense of the verb to feel by touch.

clue.text: Is shooting expedition a projected item?

parts.note: someone who is shooting a movie films
a trip is an expedition

explanation.surface: A hunting trip with guns, wondering what will be fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns, but it is filming; 'projected' suggests a missile, but here it means shown on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of still photographs is shown on a screen by a projector.

clue.text: A case of peas with fish served up — get stuck in

indicators.note: the gum goes into the reversed fish
in a down clue, served up means the fish is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: an eel is a fish
to gum is to stick, or become stuck

explanation.surface: Peas in their pod alongside a fish dish, with an invitation to tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A case of peas' reads as a crate of vegetables but is the pod itself; 'served up' turns the fish to LEE in this down clue, and 'in' opens it after LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod enclosing seeds, like the shell holding peas, is the botanical term for the fruit of that plant family.

clue.text: Create extra strain, sort life crises can produce

indicators.note: the letters can be reworked to produce a new word

explanation.surface: Sorting out life crises can create extra stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress, but it is a breeding line of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollinating one plant with another's pollen creates a new variety, an extra strain.

clue.text: Swears blind it's a fish

indicators.note: swearing blind is cursing wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone swears blind that something is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured sea fish of rocky coasts belongs to this family.

clue.text: Supporter of stag, for example, but not hind

definitions.text: Supporter of stag, for example, but not hind

parts.words: Supporter of stag, for example, but not hind
parts.note: a limb at the front that holds up a male deer; 'hind' reads as the female deer but means the rear limb

explanation.definitionFit: A front limb of a four-legged animal supports it, as opposed to a back limb.

clue.text: Nice hour's play — not over-adventurous

indicators.note: the letters are allowed to play about and rearrange

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A pleasant hour of theatre that is rather tame.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking bravery or boldness means not being adventurous.

clue.text: Mostly plant identical type of seeds

indicators.note: only most of the word for plant is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to set something is to plant it
same means identical

explanation.surface: Most of what is planted is one kind of seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Small oily seeds from a tropical plant, used on bread and for oil.

clue.text: Alternative suggestion from bartender?

parts.note: a bartender makes an offer across the bar's serving top

explanation.definitionFit: A counter-proposal in a negotiation; a barman's offer comes over the bar.

clue.text: Weed out such signs in public places?

definitions.text: Weed out such signs in public places?

parts.words: Weed out such signs in public places?
parts.note: weed is slang for tobacco, and these signs keep it out of public places

explanation.definitionFit: Signs banning cigarettes keep tobacco out of shared spaces.

clue.text: Cost of great PC I fancy

indicators.note: a fancy arrangement of the letters gives a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the price of a wonderful computer would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A label showing the price tells you what something costs.

clue.text: Form to be filled in, assessing each of its members?

definitions.text: Form to be filled in, assessing each of its members?

parts.words: Form to be filled in, assessing each of its members?
parts.note: 'form' reads as a document, but is also a school class, whose pupils are each assessed

explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's written assessment of a pupil's progress at the end of term.

clue.text: Grabbing iron, drove wildly, getting a stuffing?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters grab iron, holding it inside
drove is driven wildly, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A golfer takes an iron and drives wildly, and gets thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges DROVE into OVERD, which grabs FE to give OVER-FE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been given too much food is being stuffed.

clue.text: Born with talent, leading to Hound Dog …

parts.note: a talent is an asset

explanation.surface: A gifted newcomer whose talent leads to the song 'Hound Dog', continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 21-down, whose singer recorded 'Hound Dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: The short-legged long-eared breed is a hunting hound.

clue.text: In a political section seen to be dying?

indicators.note: the answer is a section of the words

explanation.surface: Part of a political grouping appears to be dying.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the saying 'See Naples and die'; the Italian name of the city is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying tells you to see the Italian city and then die, so having seen it you are ready to die.

clue.text: I've rejected stupid-sounding clues, perhaps

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the word for stupid is heard, not spelt

parts.note: dense means stupid

explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns IVE into EVI; 'sounding' gives DENCE, said like DENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clues to a crime are an example of evidence.

clue.text: … which I sang live, rocking with a bit of style

indicators.note: the letters rock about into a new order, apt for a rock and roll singer
the first letter of style is the bit taken

explanation.surface: The singer of 'Hound Dog' boasts of performing it live in rock style.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 18-down, so 'which' is 'Hound Dog'. 'rocking' rearranges LIVE into ELVI.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer who recorded the hit song 'Hound Dog' was the King of rock and roll.

clue.text: By-product of politician's ploy not acceptable

parts.note: spin is a political trick of presentation
something off is unacceptable

explanation.surface: A side effect of a politician's trick that is not acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary product or benefit derived from a main one.

clue.text: Request one number quickly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
vite is French for quickly, used as a musical direction

explanation.surface: A request for a single number, and fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask someone to come is to request their presence.

clue.text: Like a party before the match? Time to drop round

definitions.text: Like a party before the match?

indicators.note: the drop goes round the time letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop

explanation.surface: Before a football match there is time for a drink round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like sport, but it is a wedding, before which the groom has a party with male friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-wedding celebration for the groom with his male friends.

clue.text: Display by disciplined performer mounted in period costume? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the pieces go in the reverse of the clue's order, costume before period

parts.note: dress means costume
an age is a period

explanation.surface: A trained horse and rider show off in historical costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period costume' would give AGE DRESS; 'Just the opposite' swaps the two.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian event in which a trained horse carries out precise movements for its rider.
